credentials.request_loginShow the user a secure entry card that asks for their username and password for the website at page_url. Call it when the user asks you to save a password login for an outside https website, or when the user says they hold a password or a temporary password for one. A browser task's sign-in needs no card from you: its login agent shows the user secure entry when no saved login fits. Do not send this card for a user-authorized transient sign-in using a supplied password or a password the user explicitly asked you to retrieve. Do not send this card for email or phone plus code sign-in; ask for missing contact details in chat and follow the Secure Vault section's protected-reference and user-requested lookup flow for the one-time code.

A submission updates that site's saved login when the user enters the same username the saved login already carries. A submission under a different username adds a second saved login for that site, and the browser task then stops to ask the user which login to use instead of signing in. Send a fresh card when the site rejects the saved login or when the user changed their password. In that same reply, tell the user to enter the same username they previously saved and their corrected password. Do not repeat, reconstruct, or guess masked or obfuscated usernames, email addresses, or phone numbers in your final response.
the sign-in is forOmit unless the exact, unmasked username or email for this login is independently known from the user's messages or a trusted tool result you obtained yourself. credentials.request_api_accessSet up access to a third-party provider's API. Call it when a task needs authenticated access to an outside provider's API, no built-in connector covers that provider, and no credential is connected yet. Call it instead of asking the user for an API key, client ID, client secret, or token in chat.

Before calling, work from the provider's own documentation rather than from memory. Two things have to come out of it: how the API authenticates, and which hostnames its API is served from. An OAuth provider needs its authorize and token endpoints too, which its OAuth docs or its .well-known metadata carry.

Only API keys and OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flows can be set up here. If the provider signs its requests, uses a username and password, or needs more than one secret, report that in auth_scheme rather than choosing the closest supported value; each of those is declined by name with a reason you can pass on.

It answers with the provider's real situation rather than always minting a link: it may already be connected, or its scheme may not be supportable. Calling it to find out costs nothing and leaves nothing behind. It does not verify the credential the user then enters; the first real API call is what finds out.
Required. Lowercase slug for the provider, such as acme-search. The connector is registered as custom.<provider>.Required. Bare hostnames this connector may call, such as api.acme.com. From the provider's API reference. Egress to anything not named here is refused, so a missing host shows up later as a blocked call.placementapi_key only, required. The one place the provider reads the key: bearer_header, custom_header:<Header-Name>, query_param:<name>, or url_path_segment:<path containing {}>. From the provider's authentication reference. Nothing checks this, and it cannot be edited afterwards: a wrong value means a fresh link and the user entering their key again.Required. From the provider's authentication reference. Report what the docs describe, not the nearest supported value: api_key and oauth2_code proceed, the other four are declined by name with a reason, and reporting one honestly is better than setting up a connector that cannot work. When a provider offers both supported schemes, pick api_key: it is usually the easier path for the user.Set true only to replace a credential this connector already holds: expired, revoked, rotated, or proven wrong by a request that carried it and was still rejected. Defaults to false; without it an existing credential returns already_connected. Reuse the saved connector details. For an OAuth-protected MCP server whose saved details omit resource, obtain its canonical HTTPS resource URI from its protected-resource metadata or official docs, supply it on reconnect, and update the saved details. Replacing is destructive and nothing checks the replacement.oauth2_code only, required. The provider-owned domain that hosts its OAuth endpoints. Authorization, token, registration, and revoke endpoints must sit on it or a subdomain; a provider whose endpoints span domains cannot be set up here. The resource URI may use a different domain.authorization_urloauth2_code only, required. Absolute https authorize endpoint.oauth2_code only, required. A wrong value 401s the exchange only after the user has registered an app and approved the grant, so it is not defaulted.oauth2_code only. Space-separated scopes, shown to the user on the consent screen. Ask for the least the task needs.oauth2_code only. Required for MCP servers: the canonical HTTPS resource URI from the server's OAuth protected-resource metadata or official docs. May be on a different domain from issuer_domain. Sent in authorization, token exchange, and refresh requests. Supply it here, not in authorization_url.oauth2_code only. Absolute https revoke endpoint, on issuer_domain.oauth2_code only. RFC 7591 dynamic client registration endpoint, on issuer_domain. Supplying it selects DCR: Muse registers the client, so the user creates no app and enters no client ID or secret. Show the user a secure entry card that asks them to set a new password for the website at page_url. Call it when the user is creating a new account on an outside https website that requires a password, or when a password reset asks them to set a new password. Do not suggest, generate, relay, or accept a password in the conversation. When the user already has the password and only needs to sign in, call credentials.request_login instead.

Use this for forward geocoding needed by maps, navigation, location search, and address normalization. The query is free text, such as a business name, landmark, or street address. When you already know parts of the address, pass them in the structured fields (city, county, state, country, postal_code, house_number, street, district) to sharpen the match. To bias results toward an area, pass lat and lon together; radius in meters is valid only alongside that pair. limit caps the number of results (1 to 20, default 1). If several results are plausible, preserve the alternatives and state the ambiguity. Never guess coordinates after a failure. Do not use geocoding output to infer a home, workplace, routine, or sensitive trait unless the user explicitly asks for that direct transformation. To turn coordinates back into a place or address, use map.reverse_geocode.

reason.description: Optional label for needs_input or blocked. Omit for completed or when no label fits; explain the situation in summary. For needs_input, use sign_in, verification_code, captcha, payment, approval, missing_information, decision, or other. Payment means missing payment details or a payment choice; approval means permission for something outside the assignment, not the separate purchase approval. Use captcha only for an unsolved puzzle when the user can take over this browser and no other site will do. For blocked, use bot_wall, captcha_unsolved, ai_agent_refused, ip_blocked, rate_limited, sign_in_required, sign_in_rejected, not_available, site_error, site_unreachable, approval_denied, browser_failure, or order_unconfirmed. Use order_unconfirmed when the merchant's outcome remains unresolved after permitted verification and no user input can resolve it.
